_sources.discrepancies: NCSL lists MS as 'strict photo ID' — one of the strictest categories. SoS site confirms voters without photo ID must vote a provisional ballot and present ID before a set deadline or it will not be counted. Consistent. [2026-06-10] Corrected the 2026 primary from June 2 to Tuesday, March 10, 2026 and the primary runoff from June 23 to Tuesday, April 7, 2026, per the MS SoS 2026 Elections Calendar and FVAP (Mississippi holds its federal/state primaries in March in even years). Registration deadlines: Feb 9, 2026 (primary) and Mar 9, 2026 (runoff) per SoS. General Nov 3 confirmed (registration deadline Oct 5).

votingRules.expirationRule: Photo ID must not be expired, with limited exceptions allowed under Mississippi law. Details: https://www.sos.ms.gov/elections-voting/voter-id
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Voters without photo ID must vote provisionally and present a valid photo ID to the circuit clerk's office by noon 5 business days after the election. Alternatively, they may cast a provisional ballot and sign an affidavit at a circuit court within that window.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Mississippi prohibits use of mobile phones and other communication devices in the polling booth.
additionalRules: Open primary: any registered voter may vote in any party's primary.
Runoff rule: if no candidate receives a majority in the primary, the top two advance to a runoff. A voter who voted in one party's primary may only vote in that party's runoff.

eligibility: Will be absent from the county on Election Day

voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Must be received by the circuit clerk 5 days before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the circuit clerk by 5 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Absentee ballot must arrive at the circuit clerk by 5 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

runoffRules.ruleExplanation: Mississippi rule: if you voted in one party's primary, you can only vote in that same party's runoff. If you did not vote in the primary, you may choose either party's runoff.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Mississippi has an open primary (Miss. Code §23-15-211). Any registered voter may participate in either party's primary. If a runoff occurs and you voted in a party's primary, party-lock rules apply to the runoff.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Mississippi tiene una primaria abierta (Miss. Code §23-15-211). Cualquier votante registrado puede participar en la primaria de cualquier partido. Si hay una segunda vuelta y votó en la primaria de un partido, se aplican las reglas de bloqueo de partido.
